text:
Utah held a 75 percent "deserved to win" grade (the share of simulated replays of every shot that the team wins), and the Mammoth needed all of it. UTA led 5-2 early in the third period, then watched Pittsburgh score twice before hanging on for a 5-4 win at Delta Center.

The gap in chances was wide. UTA finished with 4.21 expected goals (a measure of shot quality) to PIT's 2.26, and out-attempted the Penguins 62 to 48. The first period tilted hardest, 1.58 to 0.60. Erik Karlsson put PIT ahead on a power-play slap shot 1:11 in, but Clayton Keller tied it at 6:00 and Kevin Stenlund made it 2-1 at 10:10. Rickard Rakell tied it again on the power play in the second, and then Nate Schmidt scored on a 2 percent chance, a slap shot that gave UTA the lead for good. Kailer Yamamoto tipped one in at 14:40, and Nick Schmaltz scored on a power play 1:36 into the third.

Pittsburgh refused to fold. Egor Chinakhov made it 5-3 at 2:55, and Declan Carlile cut it to one at 14:55. Both goalies finished below expectation, Sebastian Cossa by 1.74 goals and Arturs Silovs by 1.17. Schmidt, Stenlund and Schmaltz each had a goal and an assist and were named the game's three stars.
